title: Finitely generated ideal for a quasi-finite degree sublevel locus on an affine open
statement: Under the flat, locally finitely presented, separated, quasi-finite hypotheses and the universal degree criterion, the degree-≤r locus restricted to an affine open W is the zero locus of a finitely generated ideal of Γ(S,W).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Tag 07RZ, proof, second paragraph

proof.text: Construct I as the vanishing ideal of the preimage of the closed sublevel locus under W.fromSpec. PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus_vanishingIdeal_eq_closure and closedness show V(I) is this preimage. The affine-open zero-locus image formula identifies the range of Spec(A/I) -> S with the sublevel locus intersected with W.

On W, the lower bound r <= degree and the sublevel bound degree <= r force degree = r. Apply the universal degree criterion to Spec(A/I) -> S. Quasi-finiteness supplies quasi-compactness of f. Apply quotient-ideal fixed-degree descent to obtain J <= I finitely generated with the same degree-r base-change property.

For a point of W in the sublevel locus, membership in V(I) implies membership in V(J), since J <= I. Conversely, a point of V(J) intersect W belongs to the range of Spec(A/J) -> S; the universal degree criterion gives degree = r, hence degree <= r. This proves the unchanged conclusion with J.

proof_origin.text: Lean implementation of the stated ideal approximation route, using canonical vanishing ideals and quotient spectra.
